cells.Effect: Sets the largest number of pieces into which Tron splits the software attention work on one KV cache page (64 tokens). Different attention workers (CPU threads that compute software attention) can then run the pieces. `0` or `1` turns splitting off. The attention worker count also limits the pieces. Work for fewer than 32 tokens computed together is not split. A bad value aborts at the first forward pass with software attention work, not at startup. No flag exists. No log line shows the value.

cells.Values and default: Decimal integer of 1 or more, digits `0` to `9` only. Unit: tokens in one minibatch. Empty text, `0`, a sign, a space or a letter is rejected. Unset: 4 tokens. Empty: rejected like an invalid value.
cells.Effect: Sets the smallest minibatch that launches hardware attention early. A minibatch is a group of tokens that one forward pass computes together. At or above this size, hardware attention launches before the keys and values of the current token are saved, and below this size it launches after. The value is checked in the first forward pass, not at startup. A rejected value then logs `invalid TRON_HWATTN_EARLY_LAUNCH_MIN_B` and aborts the process. The value does not change which operations use hardware attention. Perfetto events of the category `hwattention-detail` show it as `min_b`.

cells.Values and default: Integer, parsed with `atoi`. A result above 0 forces head tiling on. Any other set value forces it off: `0`, a negative number, or text that is not a number. cells.Values and default: Number without a unit, parsed with `std::atof`. It must be 0 or above. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. Unset: `0.1`. Empty: counts as `0`.
cells.Effect: Sets how strongly each update moves the speed estimate of each worker of the shared thread pool (the worker threads for model work on the CPU) toward the mean of all workers. `0` removes this effect. The estimates split the attention work between the workers that run attention. At each update the mean of all workers gets the weight `1-exp(-value/timescale)`. The timescale is `TRON_SPEEDOMETER_TIMESCALE` or its default of 10 updates. A negative value aborts the process with `Expected prior_strength >= 0.0f`. The estimates are not used when the model config sets `pay_for_determinism`.

cells.Values and default: Number, parsed with `std::atof`. The unit is updates of the speed estimator. It must be above 0. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. Unset: `10` updates. Empty: counts as `0`, and the process aborts.
cells.Effect: Sets the time constant of the speed estimator of the shared thread pool (the worker threads for model work on the CPU). At each update, the estimator multiplies its stored measurements by `exp(-(1+p)/value)`, where `p` is `TRON_SPEEDOMETER_PRIOR_STRENGTH`. A larger value makes the speed estimates change more slowly. The speed estimates split the attention work between workers. A value of 0 or below aborts the process with `Expected timescale > 0.0f`. `TRON_SPEEDOMETER_PRIOR_STRENGTH` is divided by this value. There is one update per forward pass. A model config with `pay_for_determinism` ignores the estimates.

cells.Values and default: Integer `N`, parsed with `atol`. `N` of `0` or less turns hardware attention off. `N` above `0` turns it on. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. Unset: on from token position 127 for models generated by ingest, off for other models. Empty: off for every model.
cells.Effect: Chooses hardware attention or software attention for every eligible model. `N` above `0` also sets the first token position that hardware attention serves. That position is the smallest value `k*128 - 1` that is not below `N`: `1` gives position 127, `128` gives position 255. No command-line flag sets it. `true` and `on` count as `0` and turn it off. A model or server without hardware attention support stays on software attention. Check: the log lines `HW attention enabled for model` (field `engagement=`) and `HW attention disabled for model`.

cells.Values and default: Integer number of tree levels, parsed with `std::atoi`. The root counts as level 1. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. `0` and `1` draft no token. Unset: 2 levels. Empty: counts as `0`. No token is drafted then.
cells.Effect: Sets the largest depth of the draft tree. In speculative decoding, a draft model proposes this tree of candidate tokens, and the main model then verifies them. A draft step adds one level only while the tree is shallower than this value. It has an effect only when speculative decoding is active (see `TRON_USE_SPECULATION`). With the default `TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_SIZE` of 2 nodes, a depth above 2 levels adds no verified token. A negative number becomes a very large limit. No flag exists. No log line shows the value.
